MACASPAC Local Government and Regional Coordination Bureau Department of Budget and Management General Solano St., San Miguel, Manila Dear Director Macaspac: This has reference to your letter dated 02 June 2021 requesting for this Department's opinion regarding the legal existence of Barangay Lipunan in the City of Baguio in relation to its alleged non-existence in view of the letter dated 26 February 2021 signed by Director Marites B. Masarap, Bureau of Treasury (BTr), and confirmed by the B Tr Regional Office l. At the outset, this Department deems it imperative to stress that Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), the general law applicable to all local government units (LGU) and its local officials, sets the technical and political structure and mode of governance of all local governments, barangays included. Simply stated, the LGC is the basic law which must be considered by all local government units. In that regard, we would like to invite your attention to the pertinent provisions of the LGC in relation to the abolition of barangays, to wit SECTION 9. Abolition of Local Govemment Units. — A local qovernment unit mav be abolished when its income: population. or land area has been irreversibly reduced to less than the minimum standards prescribed for its creation under Book Ill of this Code, as certified by the national agencies mentioned in Section 7 hereof to Congress or to the sanggunian concerned, as the case may be. The law or ordinance abolishing a local government unit shall s eci the rovince i munici ali or baran a

with which the local qovernment unit souqht to be abolished will be incorporated or merqed. SECTION IO. Plebiscite Requirement. — No creation, division, merger, abolition or substantial alteration of boundaries of local government units shall take effect unless approved bv a maioritv of the votes cast in a plebiscite called for the purpose in the political unit or units directly affected. Said plebiscite shall be conducted by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) within one hundred twenty (120) days from the date of effectivity of the law or ordinance effecting such action, unless said law or ordinance fixes another date. SECTION 385. Manner of Creation. — 4 Oaranqau mav be created, divided, merged, abolished or its boundary substantially altered, bv law or bv an ordinance of the sanqquniang panlalawigan or sangguniang panlungsod, subject to approval by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite to be conducted by the COMELEC in the local government unit or units directly affected of time as may be determined by the law or ordinance creating In the case of the creation of barangays by the sangguniang panlalawigan, the recommendation of the sangguniang bayan concerned shall be necessary. Accordingly, the LGC explicitly sets forth the process or manner on how a barangay may be abolished, which shall either be by law or by an ordinance of the sangguniang panlalawigan or sangguniang panlungsod. Moreover, the LGC also requires that a plebiscite be conducted after the passage of the said law or ordinance. In other words, the residents of the barangay affected should vote if they are in favor of the abolition of the barangay. In addition, the law or ordinance abolishing a local government unit shall specify the province, city, municipality, or barangay with which the local government unit sought to be abolished will be incorporated or merged. Consequently, notwithstanding the fact that there are no more residents in the barangay or it has less than less than the minimum requirements prescribed under the LGC, there must still be a law or an ordinance to abolish such barangay as provided under the law as well as the plebiscite requirement. Correspondingly, in the case of Brgy. Bagong Lipunan in the City of Baguio, considering that no law or ordinance has been passed by the

Sanggunian Panlungsod of Baguio, nor a plebiscite conducted for the abolishment of the barangay, as declared by Baguio City Mayor Benjamin Magalong himself, we are of the view that Barangay Bagong Lipunan is still legally existing. We are also in a quandary about the BTr's basis in alleging the non- existence of Barangay Bagong Lipunan in the City of Baguio. Thus, the other remedy to abolish the barangay is for the Congress to enact a law abolishing the said barangay which is beyond the powers and function of this Department. We hope to have provided sufficient guidelines regarding the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: •ji'irh RINGAN Under cretary for Local Government LLLS/32
